- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and forecast shows strong upward bias, reduce early peaks and adjust downward mid-horizon.  
- If sentiment is negative (-1.00) and forecast is overly optimistic, suppress overshoots and shift mean toward lower range.  
- If recent history shows sharp declines, model tends to overcorrect upward — cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below recent high.  
- If forecast spikes early in horizon and true outcome follows a slow recovery, delay peak by 2–3 periods and reduce amplitude.  
- If sentiment is neutral and forecast mean is consistently above true mean, apply downward bias correction by 0.5–1.5% per period.  
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid overfitting to recent 18-day trend — smooth transitions and avoid abrupt reversals unless sentiment shifts.  
- If sentiment history is flat (all 0.00) and forecast shows high variance, reduce volatility and anchor to 3–5 period moving average of true values.
